1.explanation:
• gather/driver-test.js and gather/fake-driver.js simulate the low-level CDP driver and attachment/target flow. They’ll reveal how the driver currently ignores "Target.targetCreated/attachedToTarget" events for subframes.
• gather/devtools-log-test.js confirms how Lighthouse collects raw DevTools protocol logs, but only from the main session, so it never sees OOPIF network messages.
• gather/gather-runner-test.js exercises the overall gather pipeline (including driver.attach and network instrumentation) and will show that only the main frame is targeted.
• lib/network-recorder-test.js tests the module that processes incoming Network.requestWillBeSent/Network.responseReceived events—without OOPIF attachment there simply aren’t any events to record.
• network-records-to-devtools-log.js demonstrates how recorded network entries are converted back into DevTools log format, so you can see how missing OOPIF entries propagate through the entire trace.

Together, these files contain the code paths that must be modified to detect new Targets, call sendMessageToTarget('Network.enable') for each, and properly capture OOPIF network events.
1.bug_scenario: The reporter discovered that Lighthouse currently only instruments and listens for network events on the mainframe, and does not “discover” or attach to out-of-process iframes (OOPIFs) the way Chrome DevTools does. In the DevTools screenshot they show a sequence of CDP targets being created for an iframe (Target.targetCreated → Target.attachedToTarget) followed by calls to send Network.enable, Page.enable, and other domain-enable commands on the new sessionId. Because Lighthouse’s gatherer/driver never performs this target discovery and sendMessageToTarget flow, any network requests inside OOPIFs are simply never observed or recorded. This leads to missing network data for embedded cross-origin iframes.
